code: # Create a simplified version of a supermarket supermarket <- background(   # Shaking things up: Create a polygon environment   shape = polygon(     points = cbind(       c(0, 0, 5, 5, 10, 10),        c(0, 5, 5, 10, 10, 0)     )   ),     # Objects in the environment, consisting of    # some shelves and a gated entrance. Gates are   # again not interactable.   objects = list(     # Top shelves     rectangle(center = c(7.5, 7), size = c(0.7, 4)),     rectangle(center = c(6, 7), size = c(0.7, 4)),     rectangle(center = c(9, 7), size = c(0.7, 4)),      # Bottom shelves     rectangle(center = c(3, 2.5), size = c(4, 0.7)),     rectangle(center = c(3, 1), size = c(4, 0.7)),      # Central box     rectangle(center = c(7.5, 2.5), size = c(2, 2)),      # Cash register and gate     polygon(       points = cbind(         c(1, 2.25, 2.25, 2.5, 2.5, 1),          c(3.75, 3.75, 4.25, 4.25, 3.5, 3.5)       ),        interactable = FALSE     ),     rectangle(       center = c(3.5, 4.25),        size = c(0.25, 1.5),        interactable = FALSE     )   ),    # Entrance and exit are at the cash register   entrance = c(1, 5),    # Limited access so that agents have to pass the cash    # register beforehand   limited_access = list(     segment(from = c(1, 3.5), to = c(0, 3.5)),     segment(from = c(2.5, 4.25), to = c(3.375, 4.25))   ) )  # Plot the supermarket plot(   supermarket,    segment.hjust = 1 ) start_evacuation <- function(state) {   # Check whether the current iteration is greater than    # 100. If not, then we do not want to change the state.   if(iteration(state) == 100) {     # Delete all agents that were waiting to enter the     # space.     potential_agents(state) <- list()      # Delete all goals of the agents that are running      # around in the supermarket. This pertains to both     # the goal list and the current goal     for(i in seq_along(agents(state))) {       # Extract this agent       agent_i <- agents(state)[[i]]        # Change their current activities       goals(agent_i) <- list()       current_goal(agent_i)@counter <- 0       status(agent_i) <- "completing goal"        # Put the agent back in the list       agents(state)[[i]] <- agent_i     }      # Make sure that agents cannot be added anymore     # by lowering the maximal number of agents to 0     iteration_variables(state)$max_agents <- 0   }    return(state) } set.seed(1)  # Connect environment to agent characteristics my_predped <- predped(     setting = supermarket,      archetypes = "BaselineEuropean" )  # Run the simulation and provide our function  # to the `fx` argument trace <- simulate(     my_predped,      max_agents = 30,      add_agent = 5,      iterations = 250,      fx = start_evacuation )  # Create plots and GIF plt <- plot(     trace,      segment.hjust = 1 )  # Provide a cue of when the evacuation starts plt[[101]] <- plot(   trace[[101]],    segment.hjust = 1,   shape.fill = "red" )  # Save to a gif gifski::save_gif(     lapply(plt, print),     file.path("supermarket.gif"),     delay = 1/10 ) start_evacuation <- function(state) {   if(iteration(state) == 100) {     potential_agents(state) <- list()          for(i in seq_along(agents(state))) {       agent_i <- agents(state)[[i]]              goals(agent_i) <- list()       current_goal(agent_i)@counter <- 0       status(agent_i) <- "completing goal"        agents(state)[[i]] <- agent_i     }      iteration_variables(state)$max_agents <- 0      # Delete the limited access     limited_access(state@setting) <- list()   }    return(state) }

code: start_evacuation <- function(state) {   # Ensures the start of the evacuation and creates the variable of interest   if(iteration(state) == 100) {     potential_agents(state) <- list()          for(i in seq_along(agents(state))) {       agent_i <- agents(state)[[i]]              goals(agent_i) <- list()       current_goal(agent_i)@counter <- 0       status(agent_i) <- "completing goal"        agents(state)[[i]] <- agent_i     }      iteration_variables(state)$max_agents <- 0      # Create the times variable as a vector of 0s of the same length as the      # agents, containing their names     variables(state)$times <- numeric(length(agents(state))) |>       `names<-` (sapply(agents(state), id))   }    # Update the variables based on who is leaving the simulation   if(iteration(state) > 100) {     # Extract the times      times <- variables(state)$times       # Check whether any agent has left the simulation     ids <- sapply(       agents(state),       id     )     left <- !(names(times) %in% ids) & times == 0      # Update the times and put back in the list     times[left] <- iteration(state) - 100     variables(state)$times <- times   }    return(state) } #>  #> Precomputing edgesYour model: model ydgab is being simulated variables(trace[[251]])$times #> donzm eyqaz llyry mvzfl owfjm rbnvd kheaq oggxf dobyg senmi wvijj iypko  #>    67    23    98   113    47    80   102    19    93    41     6     3

Do this for each person separately. data <- lapply(   unique(data$passenger),   function(x) {     data <- lapply(       1:(length(bins) - 1),       function(i) {         # Select the relevant data, it being the data where the time lies within         # a particular bin and the passenger is x         idx <- data$time <= bins[i + 1] & data$time >= bins[i] & data$passenger == x         selection <- data[idx, ]          # Aggregate and return a single row of data         if(nrow(selection) > 0) {           return(             data.frame(               time = (bins[i] + bins[i + 1]) / 2,               passenger = x,               x = mean(selection$x),               y = mean(selection$y)             )           )         } else {           return(NULL)         }       }     )      # title: Interface to Minds for Mobile Agents
text: Pedestrian models popular tools investigate people navigate complex world live . Yet, current models assume pedestrians one , making solely applicable study movement behavior high-density situations like festivals sporting events, less low-density situations like supermarkets train stations. capture movement behavior low- high-density situations, Andrew Heathcote Dora Matzke recently proposed M4MA, proposing pedestrian behavior determined three levels: Strategic level: Consists agent want achieve navigate space; Tactical level: Consists reacting environment making tactical decisions regarding navigation case blockages; Operational level: Consists moment--moment step decisions agent takes, encompassing changes direction /speed lowest level. Critically, M4MAs pedestrians particular “personality” reflected unique parameters guide movement operational level. individual differences implemented two ways: Qualitative differences: pedestrian belongs particular class people, defining particular pedestrian profile one may encounter within setting interest; Quantitative differences: Within class, parameter values subject random variation, assigning pedestrian unique combination parameters.

code: setting <- background(   shape = circle(     center = c(0, 0),      radius = 2   ),    objects = list(     rectangle(       center = c(0, 0),        size = c(1, 1)     )   ),   entrance = c(-2, 0) ) plot(setting) model <- predped(   id = "my model",    setting = setting,    archetypes = "BaselineEuropean" ) set.seed(1) trace <- simulate(   model,   max_agents = 25,    iterations = 50 ) plots <- plot(   trace,   print_progress = FALSE ) gifski::save_gif(   lapply(plots, print),    file.path("readme.gif"),   delay = 1/10 ) #> [1] "/Users/nielsvanhasbroeck/Documents/UvA/Projects/Software, Pedestrian Modeling/man/figures/readme.gif"

what: An S4 Class to Represent Agents. — agent-class
title: An S4 Class to Represent Agents. — agent-class
text: Defines agent class, contains characteristics agent. characteristics time-independent (e.g., parameters set goals) others change time step simulation estimation (e.g., speed orientation).

title: An S4 Class to Represent Agents. — agent-class
text: id Character serves identifier agent. center Numerical vector two elements denoting current position agent (x y coordinate). radius Numeric denoting size agent. agents circular, equal radius agent. speed Numeric denoting current speed agent (m/sec). orientation Numeric denoting orientation agent (degrees) group Numeric indicating group agent belongs. Influences behavior agent social utility functions. status Character denoting current status agent, make next decision. one "move" (agent move another cell), "plan" (agent plan route next goal), "reroute" (agent replan route current goal), "reorient" (agent check movement options), "completing goal" (agent interact goal), "exit" (agent exit space), "wait" (agent wait another agent finish goal step way). waiting_counter Numeric defining long agent remain status "wait" triggered. start waiting period set equal number iterations agent still interact goal plus 2. cell Numeric denoting cell agent move . current_goal Object class goal-class represents current goal agent. goals List goals agent achieve. current goal included list. parameters Dataframe containing values parameters agent. contain parameters relevant utility functions (use predped::draw_parameters(1) example). color Character denoting color agent plotted. cell_centers Numeric matrix denoting positions agent may move particular iteration. utility_variables Data.frame precomputed containing values variables relevant compute utilities.

title: Constructor for the agent-class — initialize,agent-method
text: .Object class, left unspecified (see Example). center Numerical vector two elements denoting current position agent (x y coordinate). radius Numeric denoting size agent. agents circular, equal radius agent. id Character serves identifier agent. Defaults empty character, triggering random generation id. speed Numeric denoting current speed agent (m/sec). Defaults 0.1. orientation Numeric denoting orientation agent (degrees). Defaults 0. current_goal Object class goal-class represents current goal agent. Defaults placeholder class class goal-class. goals List goals agent achieve. current goal included list. Defaults empty list. group Numeric indicating group agent belongs. Influences behavior agent social utility functions. Defaults 0. status Character denoting current status agent, make next decision. one "move" (agent move another cell), "plan" (agent plan route next goal), "reroute" (agent replan route current goal), "reorient" (agent check movement options), "completing goal" (agent interact goal), "exit" (agent exit space), "wait" (agent wait another agent finish goal step way). Defaults "move". waiting_counter Numeric defining long agent remain status "wait" triggered. start waiting period set equal number iterations agent still interact goal plus 2. Defaults 0 cell Numeric denoting cell agent move . Defaults 0. parameters Dataframe containing values parameters agent. contain parameters relevant utility functions (use predped::draw_parameters(1) example). Defaults random set parameters default parameter list predped. color Character denoting color agent plotted. cell_centers Numeric matrix denoting positions agent may move particular iteration. usually provided altered user. utility_variables Data.frame precomputed containing values variables relevant compute utilities. usually provided altered user.

code: mll(   data,   parameters,   parameter_names = colnames(params_from_csv[["params_archetypes"]])[-c(1, 2)],   transform = TRUE,   bounds = params_from_csv[["params_bounds"]],   cpp = TRUE,   summed = FALSE,   ... )

title: Compute the min-log-likelihood — mll
text: data Data.frame containing least "id", "time", "x", "y", "goal_x", "goal_y", "goal_id". utility variables yet, add data.frame. parameters Numeric vector matrix containing parameters used. specified order specified "parameter_names". matrix, row contain parameters estimated instance "id" separately. parameter_names Character vector containing parameters want estimate. Defaults parameters defined params_from_csv. Whenever parameters used, excluded parameters assumed value 0. transform Logical denoting whether transform provided parameters real axis bounded scales imposed parameters within predped. Defaults TRUE. bounds Matrix containing lower upper bounds parameters first second column respectively. Additionally, rownames denote parameter certain pair represents bounds. used transform = TRUE. Defaults default bounds predped. cpp Logical denoting whether use mll_rcpp function compute min-log-likelihood. Defaults TRUE. summed Logical denoting whether sum min-log-likelihood one value per person. TRUE, get resulting summed min-log-likelihood individual correction avoid -Infs. FALSE, function instead return list vectors containing raw likelihoods (min-log-likelihoods!), allowing users specify corrections (needed). Defaults FALSE. ... Additional arguments passed add_motion_variables. typical estimation situation, motion variables already data. @return Either named vector containing summed min-log-likelihood (summed = TRUE) named list vectors raw likelihoods (summed = FALSE) per person dataset.

Order conform order list data. sizes IntegerVector containing number data points per person. Ignored summed TRUE. summed Boolean denoting whether sum min-log-likelihood one value per person. TRUE, get resulting summed min-log-likelihood individual correction avoid -Infs. title: An S4 class to Represent Lines — segment-class
text: important realize exactly determined whether agents can move segment constructing using segments environment. , consider following logic. Consider slot center circle. Furthermore consider radius circle equal size slot, orientation segment determined positions slots, look orientation location relative location . segment-class constructed, important starting point determining pedestrians can move segment. Consider another point Euclidian space, position P = (x, y). Now compute relative angle coordinate within circle defined slots. words, compute absolute angle coordinate P relative – call \(\alpha\) – subtract orientation line get relative angle within circle defined segment – call result \(\beta = \alpha - orientation\). block agent whenever \(\beta \(0, pi)\), let pass whenever \(\beta \[pi, 2 * pi]\). gain intuition : create segment vertical, lower y-coordinate (e.g., = c(0, 0) = c(0, 1)), agents blocked whenever find left segment, able pass segment whenever right segment.
